spans.s:
śū́ra, a. mighty, bold; as m. man of might,
hero. [√śū, 1188c: śūra is parallel w.
*κυ-ρο-ς, ‘mighty,’ whence τὸ κῦρ-ος,
‘might’ (cf. αἰσχ-ρό-ς w. τὸ αἶσχ-ος).]

súra, m. a god. [a pendant to asura,
formed by popular etymology from
asu-ra, as if this were a-sura, ‘non-god’
--see asura.]

súrā, f. spirituous, and esp. distilled,
liquor; brandy; liquor. [√1su, ‘express’:
cf. 1suta and soma.]

sū́ra, m. the sun. [cf. svàr, gen. sū́r-as,
‘sun’: perhaps a transfer to the a-declension,
 399.]

śū́rpa, n. a plaited basket for winnowing
grain.
sura-sattama, m. pl. the best of the gods.

su-rā́dhas, a. having goodly blessings,
bounteous.

surottama, a. subst. chief of gods. [uttama.
)

sūrí, m. (prop. impeller, inciter, i. e.) he
who engages priests to perform a sacrifice
for his own benefit and pays them for it,
a sacrifice-master; the same as maghavan
(q. v.) and the later yajamāna. [√2su,
‘impel,’ 1191.]

sū́rya, m. the sun, selection xl.; the Sun,
personified, selection xxxiii.; sūryā́, f.
 —1.
the Sun, personified as a female;
 —2. the
hymn of Sūryā's wedding, RV. x. 85, selection
lviii. [fr. svàr (sū́r), 1212a.]

sūryā-vid, a. knowing the Sūryā-hymn,
RV. x. 85.
